name: Question 14
problem:
The $3$rd term of a geometric sequence is $5$, and the $6$th term is $40.$ What is the first term of this sequence to exceed
$2\,020?$
worked_solution:
Since we are given that ${a}_{3}=5$ and ${a}_{6}=40$, we can find the common ratio $r$ of the sequence, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{n-m} & =\frac{{a}_{n}}{{a}_{m}} \\ {r}^{6-3} & =\frac{{a}_{6}}{{a}_{3}} \\ {r}^{3} & =\frac{40}{5} \\ {r}^{3} & =8 \\ r & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since ${a}_{3}=5$ and  $r=2$, we can use the $n$th term formula to solve for ${a}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {2}^{3-1} \\ 5 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {2}^{2} \\ 5 & =4{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $n$th term of the geometric sequence is

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\cdot {2}^{n-1} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{{2}^{2}}\cdot {2}^{n-1} \\  & =5\cdot {2}^{n-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want $n$th term to be greater than $2\,020.$
Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {2}^{n-3} & >2\,020 \\ {2}^{n-3} & >404 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡{2}^{n-3} & >\operatorname{log}⁡(404) \\ (n-3)\operatorname{log}⁡(2) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(404) \\ n-3 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(404)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(404)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}+3\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(404)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}+3≈11.658
$$

Therefore, the $12$th term is the first term of the sequence that exceeds $2\,020.$

Question 14
?

The 3rd term of a geometric sequence is 5, and the 6th term is 40. What is the first term of this sequence to exceed 2020?

a
the 14th term
b
the 13th term
c
the 10th term
d
the 11th term
e
the 12th term
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since we are given that a3=5 and a6=40, we can find the common ratio r of the sequence, as follows:

rn−m=anamr6−3=a6a3r3=405r3=8r=2

Now, since a3=5 and r=2, we can use the nth term formula to solve for a1, as follows:

an=a1⋅rn−1a3=a1⋅23−15=a1⋅225=4a1a1=54

So, the nth term of the geometric sequence is

an=a1⋅rn−1=54⋅2n−1=5⋅122⋅2n−1=5⋅2n−3.

We want nth term to be greater than 2020. Hence:

5⋅2n−3>20202n−3>404log⁡2n−3>log⁡(404)(n−3)log⁡(2)>log⁡(404)n−3>log⁡(404)log⁡(2)n>log⁡(404)log⁡(2)+3

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

log⁡(404)log⁡(2)+3≈11.658

Therefore, the 12th term is the first term of the sequence that exceeds 2020.
